title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: AI email classification by category and subcategory

claims.claim: The enable control is at Copilot Service admin center > Email settings > Email classification > Manage > Enable feature > Turn on email classification.

claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Email settings > Email classification > Manage > Define taxonomy > + Add', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/configure-email-classification.

claims.claim: The first high-level configuration task is defining categories and subcategories.
claims.quote: 1. Define email categories and subcategories that represent the types of messages your organization receives.

claims.claim: The second high-level configuration task is setting scope conditions.
claims.quote: 2. Specify which incoming emails to evaluate by setting scope conditions.

claims.claim: The third high-level configuration task is choosing timing and enabling classification.
claims.quote: 3. Choose when qualifying emails are classified, and then enable email classification.

claims.claim: The fourth high-level configuration task is simulation.
claims.quote: 4. Run a simulation to test the configuration against historical email and refine the taxonomy.

claims.claim: The fifth high-level configuration task is using categories downstream.
claims.quote: 5. Use the assigned email category in downstream processes, such as routing rules or automatic case creation.

claims.claim: Learn describes analysis of incoming email content.
claims.quote: Email classification analyzes the content of incoming emails and assigns each message to a configured category.

claims.claim: Classification assigns a configured category to an evaluated email even when the content does not clearly match.
